newsitem.title: UK: Urals on the slide, North Sea wet trades higher.
newsitem.headline: Urals on the slide, North Sea wet trades higher.

text.p: Sour Urals differentials in the Mediterranean appeared to tumble under pressure of first Iraqi exports, with an already-loaded cargo of the Russian grade rumoured to have traded on Tuesday at Dated Brent -$1 into Cyprus.
Traders said that prices for other December cargoes were seen headed toward this level with buying interest virtually non-existent.
"There are still six vessels still unsold and not a single buyer," said a Med refiner. "We ourselves are waiting for (Iraqi) Kirkuk."
A dozen oil companies and trading houses, nine from Europe and Russia, have so far signed deals with Baghdad to lift Iraqi crude.
At least two Med refiners were expected to sign shortly.
In West Africa, traders said the star performer was Angola's Cabinda which has been actively traded over the last week, firming differentials to around Dated Brent -85 cents.
Dealers said that Cabinda was sold out for January after good buying interest into the Far East.
"I think the Chinese have been taking in a bit," said one.
While distillate-rich Nigerian grades were sold out for early January, traders said that lighter grades were being aggressively offered for the first decade January.
They counted three Bonny Lights, two Qua Iboes and one Escravos still up for grabs. Offers for Bonny Light had slipped into the high (Dated Brent) -50s.
North Sea markets appeared steady to slightly firmer with Brent and Forties both commanding better premiums.
Brent for Dec 29-31 got Jan -12 cents and Forties moved at Dated +19 for December and +26 for an early January loader.
